claims.text: The starting HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy was produced by conventional melting and casting processing.
The baseline alloy has a quasi-static yield strength of 786 MPa.
The baseline alloy has a quasi-static compressive strength of 1314 MPa.
The baseline alloy has a quasi-static fracture strain of 13.5%.
High-temperature solution treatment will homogenize the alloy microstructure.
Aging at approximately 700 °C will produce nanoscale Ta-rich secondary phases in HfZrTiTa0.53.
The treatment will create a uniform dispersion of nanoscale Ta-rich precipitates in grain interiors and at or near grain boundaries.
The nanoscale Ta-rich precipitates will obstruct dislocation motion.
The precipitates will interact with dislocations through Orowan looping and dislocation pinning.
Precipitate-dislocation interactions will enhance dynamic strain hardening.
Enhanced dynamic strain hardening will delay the onset of adiabatic shear localization.
Delayed adiabatic shear localization will postpone catastrophic failure during high-strain-rate deformation.
The treatment will increase dynamic yield strength by approximately 10–15% relative to the stated baseline.
The treatment will increase dynamic compressive strength by approximately 10–15% relative to the stated baseline.
The treated alloy will have a longer uniform-deformation range than the baseline alloy under dynamic loading.
The treated alloy will have greater resistance to rapid strain localization than the baseline alloy.
The treated alloy will exhibit less abrupt impact-induced energy release than the baseline alloy.
The predicted effects apply in adiabatic dynamic compression at approximately 10^3–3×10^3 s^-1 and near-ambient temperature.
